page: Microsoft Azure L48aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD processor and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary differentiator of this configuration is its substantial bundled local storage capacity, providing 34557 GB across high-speed NVMe solid-state drives. The architecture is also Premium Storage capable, facilitating high-throughput input and output operations. Because the local NVMe storage is directly attached to the host hardware, it offers low latency and high bandwidth, though workloads requiring durable retention must account for the ephemeral nature of local instance disks.

Hardware resource distribution balances extensive storage capacity with large memory and compute density, eliminating external disk bottlenecks. This profile suits input-output-heavy applications that require local high-capacity scratch space, data ingestion buffers, or distributed caching. Primary workloads include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data warehousing, search index clusters, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L48aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine driven by an x86_64 AMD processor under Microsoft Hyper-V, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of memory. It features an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and is equipped with a bundled 34557 GB local NVMe SSD array alongside Premium Storage support. Designed without discrete GPU hardware, the instance prioritizes massive local storage volume and low-latency disk throughput to resolve bottlenecks common in high-volume I/O operations. The dense combination of compute, memory, and local NVMe capacity delivers high qualitative resource efficiency for data platforms operating on large physical datasets. The server is well suited for hosting distributed databases, enterprise data warehouses, big data analytics engines, and log indexing systems.
